svg.title: Four children are seen in the pediatric orthopedic clinic. Match each child with the management plan that fits the diagnosis.
svg.desc: Each plan is chosen by diagnosis and age. Ortolani plus limited abduction under 6 months is developmental dysplasia of the hip, managed with a Pavlik harness worn nearly all day; families never adjust the straps themselves. Clubfoot is corrected by serial casting started in the first weeks, with the cast changed weekly after manipulation. A moderate curve in a girl who is still growing is braced to slow progression, not simply watched. Blue sclerae with repeated low-force fractures is osteogenesis imperfecta, which needs bisphosphonates and protective handling, including manual blood pressures. The unused option describes Legg-Calve-Perthes care, which none of these children has.
